---
title: "A random-criterion representation of weighted risk"
subtitle: "4.8 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 11–12"
description: "Equality of weighted risk and risk averaged over an auxiliary criterion selected for a fixed report."
---

Weighted risk has a random-criterion representation. One auxiliary criterion is selected for the entire fixed report,
with selection probabilities equal to the error weights. Averaging its criterion-specific reporting risk gives the
same weighted risk as the direct calculation. The selected criterion applies to all units and reported pairs,
preserving its within-criterion joint law. This construction averages losses rather than target magnitudes. The
report is chosen before the auxiliary criterion is revealed; the representation does not describe a distribution
of stakeholder preferences or criterion-dependent report selection.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Weighted report.** Both calculations give risk .0933. The criterion contributions are .0453 and .0480.
  Changing the auxiliary criterion changes the evaluated column: the whole outlined column changes, while report 1/1/1/1/2/3 stays fixed.
- **Certain opposition.** The two directions each cost .5000, while withholding costs .3000. Both criteria
  distinguish the units with certainty. The same criterion choice applies to both units and every reported pair.
- **Three actions tie.** All 3 actions cost .5000. Other retained optima have different criterion-specific risks but the same weighted average. These are different reports, not
  different reports chosen after the auxiliary criterion is revealed.
- **Two against one.** The cheaper direction costs .3333, the reverse .6667, and withholding .4000. A certain
  two-against-one split can favor disclosure. The adjacent one-third boundary preset retains both actions sharing
  the minimum instead of treating equality as a strict preference.
- **Zero error weight.** The cheaper weighted direction costs .0000, although the ignored criterion’s own risk
  is 1.0000. Its selection chance is 0, so this branch contributes nothing. The vector can still be inspected
  without pretending the mixture would draw it.
- **No-cap coherence.** Among all 4,683 reports, 1/2/2/3/4/5 states 14 pairs with risk .1275. It states A above C
  with weighted error .3803 and B above D with .3813, both above τ .35. There is no grade cap in this example.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The report is selected before the auxiliary criterion; conditional on the supplied information, this auxiliary choice is independent of the target law. The mixture retains a whole within-criterion vector law, including unit dependence. Postrank’s
weak-error identity allows latent equality. The correspondence to KRW’s strict-count objective additionally
requires the same law, targets, orientation, units and feasible family, plus its affine and equality conditions.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The fixed default report reproduces the two calculations; small floating-point rounding differences do not change
their algebraic identity.

```r
library(postrank)
ev <- postrank_evaluate(c(A=1L,B=1L,C=1L,D=1L,E=2L,F=3L), pr_tutorial$two, weights=c(score_A=.5,score_B=.5), tau=.2)
sum(c(.5,.5)*ev$criterion_risk); ev$weighted_risk
```
:::

Standalone: [open this app](../../embed/criterion-mixture.html), for example `?preset=coherence&theme=dark`.
